convoLines.text: "Can we talk?" Benoit sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
You walk to the cache spot with Benoit. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"We're eating through stores faster than we replace them. Forage with me tomorrow? I know the far treeline, past the rocks."
"Pantry's thin and getting thinner. Come forage with me tomorrow — two of us can fill packs."
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. Meet me at where the camu-camu grows thick and we'll fill packs before dark."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"I can't reach this properly. Could you take a look?"
"It keeps getting worse. I can't haul or hunt with it like this — and if it festers, I'm done for. Please, clean it out and bind it tight."
Get to their side of the Haven door and stand next to them — then you can help.
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Hans is gone, Nino is gone, and Patricia is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
They nod — and keep their distance, for now.
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Maricela grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Maricela is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Sleep's gone strange. I pace while thinking at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on what's been happening."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
It owes us an explanation. I'm going to collect.
"The not-knowing is a splinter. I'm getting it out or it'll fester."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on wanting to make the System explain itself."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Okay, that's my quota of socializing."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Never mind this wound — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
Maricela has an edge today — something curdled.
"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "I dreamed Patricia was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"I'm picking up Patricia's share of the work. Someone should, and it might as well be me."
🤝 Maricela is already 👁️ Scout — that promise is theirs.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"As I said — we're still on what's been happening."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"I asked Irving about the pantry run — Irving's gone. Still need hands. Are you in?"
"I still need help with the pantry run."
Accept the forage request first. Meet at Haven at dawn on the following day.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Have you heard what they're calling The Reunion? Bao is pushing 'The Big Beast'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
"I've got things to do. People to avoid. You know."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Do you ever just need to be alone? Like, really alone?"
"I get it. Solitude's a resource too. Scarcer than food, some days. Be kind to yourself, okay?"
"I go to the treeline edge and count my breaths. Ten of them. That's my alone. Then I come back — alone is a luxury, and also a little bit a lie."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on needing to be alone."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Maricela nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"We went over this," Bao says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"See you around."
«مرحباً! ما اسمك؟»
«هذا صحيح. صحيح تماما.» They nod, holding your gaze a beat longer. "Food?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
«أنت إنسان طيب.» (you catch 'طيب' — kind) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«شكراً. حقاً، شكراً.» (you catch 'شكراً' — thanks) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «أنت... الرئيس؟» (you catch 'الرئيس' — boss)
They glance toward their own thoughts; the exchange is winding down.
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"You look handy. What did you do with your hands, before?"
"Useful. Everything useful matters now. I mean that as a compliment."
"These hands? Paramedic hands. Clipboards, mostly. Now they hold wire and wood, and they learn fast. Hands are honest that way."
"Still on what you did with your hands."
"You want me to follow you into the dark? Earn that first."
"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
"Benoit owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"I've got things to see to. Don't be a stranger."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Same time tomorrow, maybe."
«هيه... تتكلم عربي؟ لا؟ ...تباً.»
Samir has been stockpiling where nobody looks. "Take half. You've got the hands for it." (+4 wood, +4 fiber to the village stash.)
«اتفقنا.» They nod back, slowly.
«لن أنسى هذا.» A smile, tired but real.
«ما قصرت، الله يخليك.» (you catch 'ما قصرت' — much obliged) You point at yourself, then at them, then at the fire. Together. They get it.
Their gestures slow — the conversation thinning like light at dusk.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? I'm saving a candy bar for when things get better. I haven't told anyone."
They light up a little when they see you.
"Thank you. ...I needed someone to know, and I needed it to stop there."
"Water's almost gone — 0 liters. Haul the creek with me at dawn? Two buckets each, there and back."
"I know you and Benoit were close. I'm sorry."
"About what they confided — yeah, we never did get back to that."
"Sleep's gone strange. I clean up other people's messes quietly at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Hans Carter is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Hans is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.

d41: Emberhold watches to see if Haven holds without its dead. The bond is young — they're still deciding what Haven is, and grief delays the verdict. They'll test the link — count on it, unless Haven answers first: send grain (1,500 kcal), send a speaker (2 days), or let the silence answer. (Trust -8.)
d41: 🕯️ Hans Carter is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Hans kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.

d41: 🌲 Something still paces the treeline beyond the walls — The Big Beast — waiting for a dead Hans. It doesn't come in. The walls end the argument. (Haven is sanctuary. It'll still be out there when the new bearer leaves.)
d41: "Hans's gone." Maricela looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Hans." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Patricia blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Old World Caches (Level 1). You know where people hid things: under floorboards, in hollow trees, behind loose bricks.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Calming Panic (Level 1). Ground them: 5 things you see, 4 you hear, 3 you touch. Breathe with them. Slow is fast.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Tireless Stride (Level 1). You walk like water downhill — no wasted steps, no wasted breath. Every mile costs 15% less.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Reading People (Level 1). Microexpressions leak truth. Watch the eyes, not the mouth. People tell you who they are.
d41: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Deep Read! You don't just read trust — you read intent. Know what they'll do next. (Your knowledge of Reading People amplifies your open_book.)
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Hans Carter, 41 days. The mantle passes to Patricia Flores.
d41: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Patricia Flores, 28 — an emergency dispatcher. Her hands know different work now: Beast-calm, Lucky Rock, Trophy Room.
d41: ◈ The System updates its file: the new bearer <redacted> "Stalker of the Apex Predator." It had a word for this one before the Codex came.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Hans — and Hans is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: At the grave, Maricela, Bao, Irving and 6 more speak for Patricia — "Hans trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d41: The fire knew Patricia before the Codex did — her name already carried weight here.
